title: Cohomological dimension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. All sheaves below are sheaves of abelian groups. On either site, put $F[\ell^r]=\ker(\ell^r:F\to F)$ for $r\geq0$, and call $F$ *$\ell$-power torsion* if the canonical map $\varinjlim_{r\geq0}F[\ell^r]\to F$ is an isomorphism, with the inclusions as transition maps. This is the local torsion convention; no common exponent is required. Take the following suprema over $q\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ in $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}\cup\{+\infty\}$, whose empty supremum is $0$.

For a qcqs scheme $S$ and a qcqs morphism $g\colon X\to Y$, the
*$\ell$-cohomological dimensions* are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)&=\sup\{q: H^q(S_{\Proet},F)\neq0
  \text{ for some classical $\ell$-power torsion sheaf $F$}\},\\
\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)&=\sup\{q: R^qg_*F\neq0
  \text{ for some classical $\ell$-power torsion sheaf $F$ on }X_{\Proet}\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For a field $K$ we write $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(\Spec K)$.

By the cohomology comparison and the direct-image comparison these are the usual
$\ell$-cohomological dimensions computed on the étale sites, so the classical
bounds apply. If $K$ is a field with $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)<\infty$, then
$\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$ and $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)$ are finite for all
schemes $S$ and morphisms $g$ of finite type over $K$ (Stacks Project, Tag
0F10).

Here the small pro-étale site is [sk-def-pe-site], classical means [sk-def-pe-classical-definition], and qcqs and finite type have the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The notation $H^q(S_{\Proet},F)$ means $\mathcal H^q(R\Gamma(S_{\Proet},F))$, where $\Gamma$ is evaluation at the terminal object $S$; $R^qg_*F$ means $\mathcal H^q(Rg_*F)$, where $(g_*F)(V)=F(V\times_YX)$ is the direct image on the small pro-étale sites [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. Both right derived functors are as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], applied to a sheaf in degree zero. The étale notation in the comparison clause is that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. In the last sentence $g:X\to Y$ is a $K$-morphism between finite-type $K$-schemes, in the sense of [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

proof.text:
Use the small pro-étale sites of [sk-def-pe-site]: their objects are weakly étale schemes over the base, and a covering must satisfy the fpqc finite-refinement condition above each affine open, with no requirement that the whole covering family be finite. The annihilator colimits below are colimits in sheaves for this topology. Transport the allowed coefficient sheaves, taking $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Every classical abelian sheaf is $F\cong
u^*F_0$, uniquely up to isomorphism, and $
u^*$ is exact and fully faithful. In particular $
u^*(F_0[\ell^r])\cong(
u^*F_0)[\ell^r]$, by the kernel definition [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]. The adjunction also shows that $
u^*$ preserves the colimit of this countable diagram: maps from $
u^*(\varinjlim A_r)$ to $G$ are the same as compatible maps $A_r	o
u_*G$, hence as compatible maps $
u^*A_r	o G$. The colimits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], for the constant ring $\mathbf Z$ on each site. Therefore applying $
u^*$ identifies the canonical map $\varinjlim F_0[\ell^r]	o F_0$ with $\varinjlim F[\ell^r]	o F$. Full faithfulness reflects an isomorphism: lift its inverse by fullness and verify the two inverse equations by faithfulness. Thus $F$ is $\ell$-power torsion if and only if $F_0$ is. This uses the local colimit condition, not the false requirement that all sections on arbitrary disconnected site objects have finite order.

For a sheaf $F_0$ regarded as a complex in degree zero, the right-derived notation is interpreted by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], whose statement specifies the total right derived functor applied to such complexes. Then [sk-prop-sf-comparison], with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, gives $R\Gamma(S_{\Proet},\nu_S^*F_0)\simeq R\Gamma(S_{\Et},F_0)$. Taking degree $q$ cohomology identifies the two groups. Step 1 identifies exactly the permitted coefficient sheaves, so the sets of nonvanishing degrees, and hence their suprema, agree. This proves the absolute comparison clause, also for $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

For the given qcqs $g$, apply [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] to $F_0$ in degree zero and take degree $q$ cohomology. Exactness of $
u_Y^*$ from [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] gives $R^qg_{\Proet,*}
u_X^*F_0\cong
u_Y^*R^qg_{\Et,*}F_0$. The same fully faithful exact functor detects zero objects: if $
u_Y^*G=0$, its identity is zero, so faithfulness implies $\mathrm{id}_G=0$ and $G=0$; it preserves zero by additivity. Thus the higher direct images vanish in exactly the same degrees. Step 1 again identifies all permitted sheaves, proving the relative comparison clause. The qcqs hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis of the cited comparison theorem.

Let $g:X\to Y$ be a $K$-morphism between finite-type $K$-schemes. First check the geometric hypotheses explicitly. The field $K$ has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian. Every open of $X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus any morphism with source $X$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image of an affine open is an open of $X$. Apply this also to the diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ to see that $g$ is quasi-separated. The same argument for the structure maps proves that every finite-type $K$-scheme is qcqs. Clause (1) of [lem-kun-0f10] supplies a natural number $e_g$ bounding $R^qg_{\Et,*}F_0$ for every torsion abelian étale sheaf, in the convention [def-kun-cd]. Every $\ell$-power torsion sheaf is torsion: by the sheafified-colimit construction used in step 1, each section locally comes from some $F_0[\ell^r]$, and is therefore locally annihilated by the positive integer $\ell^r$. The local-section criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] implies the colimit-isomorphism condition of [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Consequently this bound applies to the sheaves of step 1. Step 3 implies $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)\leq e_g<\infty$. No assumption on $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)$ is needed for this relative assertion.

We record explicitly the coefficient condition needed for the absolute bound. For an étale abelian sheaf $G$, [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies $(G[\ell^r])_{\bar y}$ with $(G_{\bar y})[\ell^r]$, and [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits] identifies the stalk of $\varinjlim_rG[\ell^r]$ with the corresponding colimit of abelian groups. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], applied to $\mathbf Z$-modules, this is the union of the subgroups killed by powers of $\ell$. Its inclusion into $G_{\bar y}$ is an isomorphism exactly when every element is killed by such a power. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], the canonical sheaf map is an isomorphism exactly when this holds at every geometric point. If $s:S\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is qcqs and $F_0$ is $\ell$-power torsion, apply [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] with the singleton set of primes $\{\ell\}$. Each stalk element of $R^qs_*F_0$ is killed by a positive integer with all prime divisors equal to $\ell$; such an integer is $\ell^r$ (including $1=\ell^0$). The criterion just proved shows that every $R^qs_*F_0$ is $\ell$-power torsion in exactly the same sense as $F_0$.

proof.text: Suppose $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)<\infty$ and let $S$ be finite type over $K$. Its structure morphism $s:S\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a morphism between finite-type $K$-schemes. Clause (1) of [lem-kun-0f10], in the convention [def-kun-cd], supplies $e_s\geq0$ with $R^qs_*F_0=0$ for all torsion $F_0$ and $q>e_s$. The Noetherian-source argument in step 4 proves that $S$ and its structure morphism $s$ are qcqs, so the comparison of step 2 and the preservation theorem of step 5 apply. By step 2 choose $c\geq0$ with $H^p(K_{\Et},G)=0$ for $p>c$ and all $\ell$-power torsion $G$. For any $\ell$-power torsion $F_0$ on $S_{\Et}$, step 5 shows that $G=R^qs_*F_0$ has this property for every $q\geq0$. Both hypotheses of [lem-sc-leray-vanishing-bound] now hold for $s,F_0,c,e_s$, so $H^n(S_{\Et},F_0)=0$ for $n>c+e_s$. Step 2 yields $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)\leq c+e_s<\infty$. This does not replace finite $\ell$-dimension of $K$ by the stronger hypothesis of finite torsion dimension. Empty schemes and morphisms with empty source give only zero cohomology, consistent with the empty-supremum convention.
